marks.gloss_en: דתניא, רבי אליעזר אומר: שלש משמרות הוי הלילה -- the baraita corroborates that R' Eliezer holds three watches
the night consists of three watches
the night consists of four watches (proposed as what R' Eliezer might hold)
the signs: first watch -- a donkey brays; second -- dogs howl; third -- an infant nurses and a wife converses with her husband
he counts the starts of the watches (rejected: the first watch's start needs no sign -- it is simply evening)
he counts the end of the first watch, the start of the last, and the middle of the middle
the use of the last watch's sign: one sleeping in a dark house rises and recites the Shema when the wife converses and the infant nurses
